record.title: M2.5 ISO metric threaded joint — 60 degree profile, 0.45 mm coarse pitch

joins.a: external ISO metric M2.5 thread (interface name: thread_ext) — a cap screw or stud
joins.b: internal ISO metric M2.5 thread (interface name: thread_int) — a tapped hole, or the Microduck's head-close case: a self-tapped printed post (Ø2.100 x 11.200 with a Ø2.800 x 0.800 lead-in, MEASURED on top_head_shell, out/verify/manufacturing_partial.json)

record.dof_left_why: A tightened threaded joint is a clamp, not a bearing: the preload closes all six degrees of freedom between the joined faces by friction at the interface. UNTIGHTENED the same pair leaves one helical DOF (rotation about z coupled to translation along z at 0.45 mm/turn) and mate() reports that when params['state'] == 'loose'. The default is the tightened joint because that is what an assembly means by 'screwed'. Same physics as connection:threaded-m2 and connection:threaded-m3; only the pitch changes the coupling ratio.
record.standard: ISO 68-1 (basic profile) / ISO 261 (general purpose coarse thread series) / ISO 262 (selected sizes) / ISO 898-1 (property classes)
record.standard_why: ISO 68-1 fixes the 60 degree triangular basic profile and therefore H = 0.8660*P. ISO 261 fixes that the coarse pitch for a 2.5 mm nominal diameter is 0.45 mm — cross-checked against ce-cad/cecad/fasteners.py line 58, the M2.5 row (pitch 0.45, tap drill 2.05, close/normal/loose clearance 2.70/2.90/3.10) this workshop already drills against, and against ce-parts/screw-m2.5-iso4762 on the workshop shelf (an ISO 4762 length family with 14 lengths verified on a fetched page). None of the standards documents was FETCHED in this session: what WAS done is that the ISO 68-1 profile relations were used to DERIVE d2 = 2.207716, d3 = 1.947909, D1 = 2.012861 and As = 3.390804 mm2, and all four reproduce the published M2.5 table figures (2.208 / 1.948 / 2.013 / 3.39) to <= 0.0009 mm and 0.0009 mm2 — an independent check, since none of the published figures was used to produce them. Run compat.py to reprint the derivation; the artifact is evidence/m2p5-thread-derivation.json.
record.adds_parts_why: screw-m2.5-iso4762 (hex socket head cap, ISO 4762, a length family with 14 sourced lengths 3–30 mm) is the only M2.5 fastener family with a folder on any reachable shelf — checked 2026-09-03 by listing the workshop ce-parts/ (no nut-m2.5, no insert-m2.5 exists), and TRIAD.md makes a dangling ref a FAIL, never a warning. So mate() maps provider 'socket_head_cap' to this ref, maps 'tapped_hole'/'self_tapped_boss' to no part (the thread is cut into part B itself — the Microduck's head-close case, Ø2.100 printed posts measured on top_head_shell), and REFUSES any other provider by name instead of inventing a ref.
record.why: The GEOMETRY of the pair is PASS and it is derived, not recalled: from the ISO 68-1 basic profile with P = 0.45 mm, d2 = 2.207716 mm, d3 = 1.947909 mm, D1 = 2.012861 mm and As = 3.390804 mm2, and all four reproduce the published M2.5 figures (2.208, 1.948, 2.013, 3.39) that were not used to produce them — run `python3 compat.py` to watch the four PASS lines. THE SIZE IS THE ROBOT'S OWN, and it is the minority size: SPEC.md section 4's hole census reads four populations off Pollen's meshes (Ø2.2 clearance x77, Ø4.4 c'bore x28, Ø1.6 tap x20 — all three the fasteners.py M2 figures — and Ø2.7/2.8 x20, which are the fasteners.py M2.5 close and normal clearances and are what docs/BOM.md section 4 buys 'M2.5x6 x20' for). Two of those twenty positions are measured rather than inferred: the three head-close screws (Ø2.695 clearance into Ø2.100 x 11.200 posts, out/verify/manufacturing_partial.json) and the four compute-board mount holes (Ø2.8140, measured off Radxa's own §4 drawing, part:radxa-zero-3w cad/interfaces.json). The TORQUE of the pair is CANNOT DETERMINE and stays that way: no friction coefficient has been measured in this workshop (threaded-m2 and threaded-m3 record the identical refusal), and the PLA self-tapped case adds a second unmeasured number — pull-out of an M2.5 formed thread in a printed Ø2.1 pilot. compat() therefore returns PASS on fit and CANNOT DETERMINE on preload/engagement unless the caller supplies measured values; both refusals are ledger rows.

joint.default_state: tight. params['state'] == 'loose' is the other case and mate() reports it.
joint.why: holds_by: preload — record.dof_left_why is the citation: 'the preload closes all six degrees of freedom between the joined faces by friction at the interface'. Preload, not friction: friction is the mechanism, preload is the source. rating: all three numbers MISSING and refused rather than defaulted — no friction coefficient and no PLA pull-out has been measured in this workshop, and compat.py's preload check says so with the formula it would use. THE LOOSE STATE IS A COUPLING: mate() returns dof_left ['helical_about_z'] for params['state'] == 'loose', which maps to rz free plus a couples entry {of: tz, per: rz, mm_per_rev: 0.45} — the ISO 261 coarse pitch for nominal diameter 2.5 mm, stated in the modules as PITCH_MM and cross-checked against the cecad fasteners.py M2.5 row.
